title: From a 2–3 Exit to a Team Record: Jiao Er's Remarkable 2026 Zijing Cup Journey
content:
After the elimination match, we were packing our rackets and preparing to go home. Then the organizers revealed a surprising lineup error by the Xi'an Jiaotong–Fudan team: its third men's doubles pair had a higher rating than its second men's doubles pair. D3 was awarded to us. Jiao Er, seemingly already out, came back to life and advanced to the main draw.

For the first time, we entered as a single-school team without outside reinforcements. Four consecutive qualifying matches nearly exhausted our core players. Qing'er and Jess had to retire from women's doubles because they were physically spent. In the main draw, we strategically conceded one women's lineup slot to give more teammates a chance to play and gain match experience.

Unexpectedly, it worked. David and Jay at D1 won all five deciding “golden points” against their opponents, taking down Huazhong University of Science and Technology's top player, rated UTR 7.6. Jiajing and Yaofeng came back from two games down to force a deciding game. Even captain Yuan Hu, who plays only a handful of times a year, quickly found his rhythm.

The most thrilling moment came in the crossover elimination match against Tsinghua's second team. Qing'er and Jessie handled the pressure to win women's doubles 4–1, 4–2. In men's doubles, Shuo Liu played through injury, eventually hopping on one leg to get into position and battling to a match-tiebreak victory. Although a loss at D2 ultimately meant a 2–3 overall exit, everyone played across seven team matches, and we achieved the best result in team history.
